01 / A library that remembers.

Library · Search · Collection

01

Library

/library

Recognize a collection by its material, then return to the reference that matters.

9:41

Library

Collections

402 × 874 pt · Library

Design notes / 01

  1. 01
    Recognition before organization

    Three real references form a collection’s contact sheet. The name and count live below it, without a surrounding card or decorative folder.

  2. 02
    Search belongs to navigation

    The large title and search field collapse together on scroll in the native app. Pull down to recover search; its scope remains the entire private library.

  3. 03
    Capture is always one step away

    A stable three-item tab bar makes capture reachable from either end of the library. Capture presents a task, then returns to the same browsing position.

  4. 04
    Status only when it earns space

    A small upload count appears while work is outstanding. It opens the queue; when everything is saved, it disappears. The plus creates a Collection, not an ambiguous menu.

Try it. Open a collection, tap Search or Capture, or create a sample collection. Scroll within the phone to see all collections.

402 × 874 pt · Library / Search

Design notes / 02

  1. 01
    Show the reason for a match

    A compact excerpt tells you whether a title, note or tag matched. The thumbnail stays large enough to recognize; the result is always a Reference.

  2. 02
    Literal, explainable retrieval

    The current web mock uses case-insensitive substring matching over loaded titles, notes, tags, source, filenames and pin captions. This native search surface preserves that explainable model; it adds no ranking or semantic behavior.

  3. 03
    Keep the collection in context

    Collection names remain visible in results. Opening an item should return to this exact query and result position, rather than resetting to the library.

  4. 04
    A useful empty state

    Keep the query editable when no results match. Don’t suggest AI search or fabricate nearby results. VoiceOver announces the result count after input settles.

Try it. Change “matcha” to “Yokó”, “062.jpg”, or a word with no matches. Switch between reference and collection results.

Global native search is proposed; existing field coverage is preserved

moode-matcha

160 references
Newest first

402 × 874 pt · Collection

Design notes / 03

  1. 01
    Density without decorative framing

    A three-column contact sheet favors scanning. Narrow gutters separate the images; a list alternative exposes titles when text is a better retrieval cue.

  2. 02
    A direct spatial transition

    Open from the tapped thumbnail into the full image. Native dismissal returns to that thumbnail and preserves the collection’s precise scroll position.

  3. 03
    Description is useful, never required

    The description is an editable sentence in the header, not a large empty panel. It helps a collection remain understandable after the original project has faded.

  4. 04
    Publishing is a separate decision

    Private is the default. Collection actions can create a read-only, unlisted Board only after a publication preview. Capture never silently changes sharing.

Try it. Toggle grid/list, edit the description, or inspect the private-sharing control. Open the first reference.

402 × 874 pt · Reference

Design notes / 04

  1. 01
    The image is the destination

    No tab bar, metadata form or floating panel competes with the reference. Show the whole image at rest; preserve original proportions and offer pinch to inspect detail.

  2. 02
    Paging and zoom have different jobs

    Swipe horizontally to page only when the image is at its resting scale. While zoomed, a drag pans the current image. Visible previous/next controls provide a non-gesture alternative.

  3. 03
    Meaning stays attached

    Numbered pins live in normalized image coordinates, not viewport coordinates. Their 44-point hit regions may exceed the visible marker; VoiceOver identifies number and caption.

  4. 04
    Recover the browsing context

    Native dismissal should follow the finger, transfer release velocity and remain interruptible. Returning restores the source thumbnail; Reduce Motion uses a short crossfade.

Try it. Select either pin, inspect file facts, or use the paging arrows. The browser demonstrates selection and paging, not native zoom or gesture physics.

402 × 874 pt · Reference / Pin selected

Design notes / 05

  1. 01
    One compact inspector

    The chosen caption occupies a stable area below the image. It doesn’t float over the detail you are trying to see, and a pin tap never launches a full editing task.

  2. 02
    Selection is a shared identity

    The enlarged marker, inspector number and caption change together. Color is unnecessary: number, outline and scale make the relationship legible.

  3. 03
    Preserve image geometry

    Selecting a marker does not recrop or jump the image. If zoom is needed, a native fit adjustment must keep the selected location visible above the inspector.

  4. 04
    Long captions remain readable

    The inspector can grow to a larger native sheet detent when text size or content demands it. VoiceOver exposes a sequential annotation list with selection announcements.

Try it. Tap 01 or 02 and watch the caption change. Edit updates the selected caption locally.

402 × 874 pt · Add annotation

Design notes / 06

  1. 01
    One tap establishes the anchor

    Enter Add Pin, then tap the image. A marker appears on touch-up and a light selection haptic acknowledges placement. Ordinary viewing taps do not create accidental annotations.

  2. 02
    An immediate, focused thought

    Bring the caption input to the keyboard while preserving the anchor above it. Done commits the draft; it never opens another modal confirmation.

  3. 03
    Fast does not mean irreversible

    Cancel removes an empty draft. A nonempty draft survives interruption and is offered again on return. After commit, Undo removes the pin without disturbing the image.

  4. 04
    A native geometry problem

    Keyboard avoidance must operate on the rendered image bounds, including any letterboxing. Reposition uses normalized image coordinates. Larger type may require a taller editor.

Try it. Move the draft pin by tapping the image, edit the caption, then tap Done. This browser draft is session-only.

Keyboard, haptics and draft persistence need native validation

402 × 874 pt · Capture

Design notes / 07

  1. 01
    Capture is a short-lived task

    The Library tab keeps its place while Capture is presented. Cancel returns there; Keep returns with the new reference visible. A mode is unnecessary once the job is done.

  2. 02
    Two clear sources

    Take a photo opens the native camera; Browse opens the system photo picker. The recents strip assumes Photos access already granted and is omitted otherwise.

  3. 03
    A destination, not a prerequisite

    Default to the collection capture was opened from, then the last valid destination. A first-use library offers a clearly named collection before capture; metadata is always optional.

  4. 04
    Permission at the moment of intent

    Ask for camera access only after Take a photo. Support limited Photos access and a permission-denied path back to the system picker without an empty or broken capture screen.

Try it. Choose a recent image and continue. Camera and Browse explain the intended native handoff; this study does not request device permissions.

402 × 874 pt · Capture review

Design notes / 08

  1. 01
    Image and destination are enough

    Keep is available before any optional field is opened. The filename remains the default title. Optional title entry is a proposed native addition; title editing is not currently built. Notes and tags remain optional.

  2. 02
    A progressive second layer

    Title, note and tags live behind Add details. Expand them only when the user has a thought worth capturing. Native keyboard movement keeps the primary action reachable.

  3. 03
    Acknowledge a durable save

    “Kept” means the image and destination have reached durable local storage. Only then dismiss. Upload can continue later, but a local write failure must keep the review open.

  4. 04
    Give the action an exit

    After saving, return to the originating collection and offer a brief Undo. Prevent repeated taps from enqueuing duplicates; changing the destination remains possible in the reference.

Try it. Expand optional details, change the collection, and Keep. A local confirmation demonstrates the intended handoff; no image is uploaded.

Local durability and upload behavior are proposed, not implemented

402 × 874 pt · Share extension

Design notes / 09

  1. 01
    Finish in the host app

    The system share sheet hands an image or supported preview to Kept. The extension needs only a thumbnail, a destination and Keep; it does not open the full library.

  2. 02
    Make the default legible

    The last valid collection is visible and changeable. A stale or deleted destination requires a replacement, rather than silently saving somewhere unexpected.

  3. 03
    Save before dismissing

    Copy the attachment and queue record into shared local storage before confirming. Then return to Safari or Photos. Opening Kept later reveals the pending reference and upload state.

  4. 04
    Handle the real extension limits

    A URL alone does not promise an image. If the host provides none, say so and offer guidance. Signed-out, unsupported-type, storage-full and network-offline paths must preserve a recoverable route.

Try it. Change the collection, add a note, then Keep. The confirmation explains what happens after the extension closes.

Extension lifecycle and shared storage must be tested on device

402 × 874 pt · Upload queue

Design notes / 10

  1. 01
    Local save and remote upload differ

    A saved reference is immediately browseable from its local image copy. Uploaded means the server has acknowledged the file; the interface must not confuse these guarantees.

  2. 02
    One compact exception surface

    Queued, uploading, uploaded and failed are individual rows. A completed row is temporary; successful history clears so this never grows into a sync dashboard.

  3. 03
    Recover the specific failure

    Retry acts on one item and preserves its destination, caption and tags. Authentication failures route to sign-in; storage failures explain the required action instead of retrying forever.

  4. 04
    Background work is best effort

    Persist queue state across termination, use bounded retries and reconcile on launch. iOS may defer or suspend transfers; the product must not promise an immediate background finish.

Try it. Retry the failed upload. It returns to Queued and does not falsely report success.

Persistent queue and background transfer design require native proof

moode-matcha · Kept by Briana

Read-only collection

402 × 874 pt · Board

Design notes / 11

  1. 01
    A published view of a Collection

    The Board has no editing controls, capture tab or social counters. Larger two-column imagery and a quiet byline shift the emphasis from working to viewing.

  2. 02
    Unlisted is not private

    Anyone with the URL can view an active Board and forward it. Make this explicit at publication. Turning off the Board revokes the link without deleting the Collection.

  3. 03
    Preview what leaves the library

    Default proposal: publish images, titles and the collection description. Keep private notes, pins, tags, filenames and source metadata out unless a separate explicit policy is approved.

  4. 04
    A viewer without a workspace

    Tap an image to open a read-only lightbox, then page through the sequence. Closing restores the exact grid position. No sign-in should be required just to view an unlisted Board.

Try it. Open any image, page through the lightbox, then close. The Share control shows the proposed link policy without publishing anything.

Publication fields, live updates and revocation semantics need approval

402 × 874 pt · Sign in

Design notes / 12

  1. 01
    Familiarity is the design

    Persistent field labels, username and password, one Continue action. The wordmark appears at the entrance and then yields to the library’s content.

  2. 02
    A required second step

    Successful credentials continue into two-factor verification. Do not show the private library before both factors succeed or invent alternative sign-in providers.

  3. 03
    Let the system help

    The native implementation should support Password AutoFill, password managers and an appropriate keyboard. Validation errors preserve the username and explain the next step without exposing account existence.

  4. 04
    Keep invitation separate

    Request an invite is available without turning authentication into a waitlist landing page. Session expiry and connectivity errors should preserve a recoverable sign-in path.

Try it. Use sample values only. Continue advances to the illustrated two-factor screen. Nothing is transmitted or retained.

402 × 874 pt · Two-factor

Design notes / 13

  1. 01
    One field, six digits

    A single semantic input supports paste, keyboard entry and one-time-code AutoFill. Avoid six independent boxes that break paste or make VoiceOver navigation tedious.

  2. 02
    Treat enrollment as a real state

    A verified first-time user connects an authenticator, confirms a code and stores recovery codes before continuing. The key is shown only in that authenticated setup context.

  3. 03
    Recovery should be discoverable

    Offer a recovery-code path alongside verification. Describe unavailable recovery through the actual support policy; never invent bypasses or imply an admin can retrieve a secret.

  4. 04
    Be honest about the assumption

    The current-state brief confirms password + TOTP as the plan. The web MFA screen remains a placeholder. This study designs verification and enrollment; recovery codes still require an agreed backend policy.

Try it. Enter any six digits to demonstrate continuation, or inspect the recovery and enrollment states. No authentication is performed.

TOTP is planned; recovery-code support is a proposal

402 × 874 pt · Request an invite

Design notes / 14

  1. 01
    Only what is needed

    Name and email are required; the open question is explicitly optional. Clear labels remain after typing, with appropriate native keyboards. The optional response retains the current 500-character limit.

  2. 02
    A restrained confirmation

    After a successful server response, replace the form with a calm received state. Avoid scarcity claims, queue ranks and promises about when access will arrive.

  3. 03
    Failure stays recoverable

    A network error retains the entered values and offers Retry. Rate limits or existing requests should use neutral copy that does not expose account membership.

Try it. Submit sample details to see the illustrated confirmation. This artifact does not send an invite request.

Account

Put conventional controls where people already know to look.

9:41

Account

BW
Briana

Private library · @briana

KEPT / iOS STUDY · 0.1

402 × 874 pt · Account

Design notes / 15

  1. 01
    Settings should be unsurprising

    Use native grouped rows and disclosure navigation. Identity, security and appearance form one group; publishing and portability form another.

  2. 02
    Boards are administered here

    A small list shows which collections are published and allows revocation. Publishing is not a primary tab and never becomes the organizing principle of the library.

  3. 03
    Protect unfinished local work

    Before sign-out, inspect unsynced image copies. Explain what remains on the device and offer to wait or retry. Account switching must not attach the old account’s queue to a new owner.

  4. 04
    Conventional does not mean fixed

    Use system text styles, 44-point minimum targets and adaptable row heights. Honor system appearance and accessibility preferences; validate large text natively.

Try it. Open security, Boards, appearance, or Sign out to inspect the supporting states.

DESIGN DECISIONS

What this direction commits to.

These are design hypotheses, with confidence tied to the product model in the supplied brief. The current-state briefing has been reviewed. TOTP and literal search align with the plan; publication-field policy, recovery codes and native local durability still require decisions.

DecisionRationaleConfidenceValidate in a native prototype
Collection contact sheetsRecognize content before reading names; avoid decorative app cards.HighTest recognition against a single cover and text list with real libraries.
Reference as a full-image destinationKeep the original and its annotations spatially connected.HighShared-element opening, pan vs. paging, and restoring the source grid position.
Stable pin inspectorA selected note must not cover the detail it explains.MediumCaption length, one-handed reach, large text and sheet detents.
Explicit Add Pin modeOne tap places a point without making normal inspection destructive.MediumPlacement speed versus accidental pins; discoverability and undo.
Capture as a presented taskA short capture returns to the same collection and scroll position.MediumCamera warmup, limited Photos, repeated capture and first-use destination.
Local save before uploadFast confirmation must represent a real, durable save.HighDisk-full, termination, extension expiry, account changes and network recovery.
Minimal Board publicationImages and titles can be shared without leaking private working notes.ProposedConfirm published fields, update semantics, unlisted access and revocation.
Authenticator verificationUse a conventional required second factor with accessible code entry.ProposedValidate TOTP enrollment, errors, recovery policy and gated access.

The HTML establishes hierarchy, connected states and decision logic. None of the interactions below is considered solved by this artifact. Checkboxes are review aids only; they are not claims that native validation has passed.

CONTEXT & HANDOFF

Product model: Library → Collection → Reference, with image, notes, tags, spatial pins and file/source facts. Publishing a Collection as an unlisted, read-only Board is optional. The Reference remains the primary unit of meaning.

Reviewed: the supplied product brief and project current-state briefing, Kept’s original iOS wireframes, the supplied mobile quality reference, and the local apple-design skill. The KEPT-STORAGE destination was empty when inspected and has not been modified. Figma work is deferred until this HTML is approved.

Authoritative context reviewed: docs/KEPT-CURRENT-STATE.html, dated 20 September 2026, located in the project beside the supplied image folder. The web app is entirely mocked; native capture, durable background upload and real external Board sharing are planned. TOTP is planned, substring search exists, and imported titles are currently numbered. The importer retains resized JPEG copies, not originals. This study preserves those distinctions. The dashboard screenshot was not supplied; the numbered annotation system follows the brief.

Reference imagery: 12 images embedded directly from the user-supplied kept-design/public/collections/moode-matcha/full folder: 007, 017, 027, 033, 062, 068, 075, 092, 104, 111, 118 and 127. Image content and branding belong to their respective creators. Collection arrangements, captions, tags, dates and counts outside the supplied collection are demonstration content, not imported product data. No generated sample photography is used in this artifact. Readable reference titles and optional title entry illustrate a native proposal; the current import uses numbered titles.

Interaction boundary: all state is local to this page session. Reload resets it. Study navigation moves between annotated screens. Image zoom, continuous gestures, haptics, system permission prompts, authentication, storage and background transfers require a native implementation; the browser is not proof of those behaviors.

Craft: system typography, neutral chrome, meaningful image color, 44-point interaction targets, clear pressed states, keyboard-accessible controls and reduced-motion support. No external fonts, scripts, libraries, requests or build step.
